text: The first time the Rus met the Mongols was in twelve twenty-three, at a river called the Kalka.
The princes of Kievan Rus rode out together for once. And it went... very badly.
[wincing] Their first team-building exercise. Total disaster.
Then the Mongols vanished back into the steppe. For fourteen years, nothing.
And in twelve thirty-seven, they came back. This time, led by Batu Khan, grandson of Genghis Khan.
City after city fell. Ryazan. Vladimir. In twelve forty, the jewel of the whole land, Kyiv, was burned to the ground.
[quietly] Remember Kyiv? The rich city on the trade road? Gone.
The Mongols didn't stay to rule the forests themselves. They set up a state on the Volga called the Golden Horde... and turned the Russian princes into their tax collectors.
If you wanted to rule a Russian city, you had to travel thousands of kilometres to the Khan, bow, bring gifts... and ask for a permission slip.
[nervous] Great Khan, I humbly ask to rule my little city.
[bored] Did you bring the tax?
Every last coin.
And the extra tax?
[pause] There's an extra tax?
[smiling] There is now.
This lasted about two hundred and forty years. Russians call it the Mongol yoke.
And here's the twist. One small, unimportant town got very good at this game: Moscow.
Its prince, Ivan the First, collected the Khan's taxes so well that people called him Ivan Kalita. Ivan Moneybag.
[holding up a coin pouch] Great nickname. Terrible for your popularity.
Moscow kept a slice of the money, bought up land, and slowly swallowed its neighbours. The head of the Church even moved there.
Moscow had learned the Mongols' best lesson: one ruler, total control, and everyone pays.
In thirteen eighty, a Moscow prince, Dmitry Donskoy, beat a Mongol army at Kulikovo Field. The Horde came back two years later and burned Moscow anyway.
[sighing] One step forward, one city on fire.
The real end came in fourteen eighty, under Ivan the Third. A Mongol army and a Moscow army met on opposite banks of the Ugra River... and stared at each other. For weeks.
Then the Mongols turned around and went home. No great battle. The yoke just... ended.
[shrugging] History's most awkward staring contest.
Ivan the Third tripled Moscow's land. He married Sophia, niece of the last emperor of Constantinople, and took the empire's symbol: the double-headed eagle.
Moscow now called itself the Third Rome. Chaos had produced... total control. Again.
